text:
Dougie Hamilton is having the kind of season that looks quiet on the scoresheet and solid everywhere else. The 33-year-old is playing nearly 21 minutes a night for New Jersey, and at five on five the Devils take 57% of both the shot attempts and the expected goals with him on the ice. He has 10 points in 22 games, right on his rate from last season.

The flag on him is luck. New Jersey has scored five fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own shooting is at 3.6% on 55 shots, under the range we'd expect from a defenseman with his shot. Those things tend to even out, and when they do, the points usually follow.

Evolving-Hockey had him 41st among 215 defensemen last season, most of it on the power play, facing top competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a defensive note people don't associate with him: he stopped 18% of the entries aimed at his blue line, against 11% for a typical defenseman. We'd watch his power-play time; he has just one power-play point so far.
headline: Dougie Hamilton's numbers are better than his points
